clue.text: Dirty ancient moat in ruins

indicators.note: something in ruins has been wrecked, so the letters of these two words are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A tumbledown castle's old moat, choked with filth, sits among the ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty' looks like an adjective describing the moat, but it is a verb defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To dirty something is to pollute or foul it, the verb's ordinary synonym.

clue.text: Predicting the outcome of vocation

definitions.meaning: as in shouting heads or tails before a coin lands
a strong sense of being drawn to a particular career, often the priesthood

explanation.surface: Forecasting how a career will turn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling heads at a toss predicts the result, and a calling is also a vocation or life's work.

clue.text: Martial artists primarily needed in shark film, not Western

indicators.note: primarily takes only the first letter of the word needed
not says the abbreviation for western is taken out of the film title

parts.note: Jaws is Spielberg's 1975 film about a great white shark

explanation.surface: Kung fu fighters are needed in a shark movie rather than a cowboy picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western' looks like a film genre beside 'film', but it is just W.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninjas were Japanese covert agents trained in ninjutsu, a martial art, so they are martial artists.

clue.text: Believe in West Ham pairing from the beginning

definitions.meaning: in Cockney rhyming slang of East London, home of West Ham, 'would you Adam it?' means would you believe it
the first couple in the Book of Genesis

explanation.surface: A football fan's faith in a West Ham partnership that has lasted since the start.
explanation.walkthrough: West Ham is an East London football club; Cockney rhyming slang swaps a word for a phrase rhyming with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang uses the biblical first couple for believe, and Genesis makes them humanity's first pair.

clue.text: Dope, lamebrain, fool — not all there!

indicators.note: not all there says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A string of insults for an idiot who is a bit simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' and 'not all there' seem to extend the insults; dope here is slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for inside information, as in 'the latest dope on the race'.

clue.text: Perfumed woman leaving case in lorry

indicators.note: in says the trimmed woman goes inside the lorry

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry

indicators.note: the word woman leaves its outer letters, its case, behind

explanation.surface: A scented woman abandons her suitcase in a truck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving case' looks like a woman walking off without her luggage; it strips W and N from WOMAN, leaving OMA. ARTIC is British for an articulated lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Aromatic means having a pleasant, fragrant smell, much like perfumed.

clue.text: Commend hospital department getting on top of fungal disease

indicators.note: in a down answer, the department sits above the disease

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
rust is a fungal disease of plants

explanation.surface: Praise for a hospital unit beating a fungal infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commend' looks like praise, but here it means hand over for safekeeping.
explanation.definitionFit: To commend something to someone's care is to hand it over trustingly, the old sense of commit.

clue.text: East European, not fan, regularly dismissed Italian food

parts.note: a Pole is a native of Poland, in eastern Europe

indicators.note: every other letter of the words not fan is thrown out, leaving the alternate letters that remain

explanation.surface: Someone from Eastern Europe who dislikes it keeps waving away an Italian dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly dismissed' drops O, F and N from NOTFAN, keeping N, T, A.
explanation.definitionFit: Polenta is a cornmeal porridge from northern Italy, a classic Italian dish.

clue.text: Mushy peas I resist in shops

indicators.note: mushy peas are mashed to a pulp, so these letters are mashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone resists the mushy peas on offer in the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: Mushy peas are a British side of mashed marrowfat peas, served with fish and chips.
explanation.definitionFit: Patisseries are bakeries selling pastries and cakes, a particular kind of shop.

clue.text: Loud yob turned on defiant person

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical marking for loud
a lout is a boorish yob

indicators.note: turned says the short word for on is read the other way round

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A noisy thug rounds on someone who flouts the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes ER from RE, the Latin-derived 'on the subject of'.
explanation.definitionFit: One who openly disregards rules or authority is defiant, and that is what this agent noun describes.

clue.text: Unmerciful soldiers scrap on eastern ship

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British Army corps of soldiers
a morsel is a tiny scrap of food
SS, steamship, prefixes a ship's name

explanation.surface: Pitiless troops fight over scraps on a ship from the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorseless means relentless and without pity, synonymous with merciless.

clue.text: Decorate a foul docked boat

parts.note: to trim a dress or tree is to decorate it

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the last letter of the synonym for foul is removed

parts.note: rank means foul-smelling

explanation.surface: Someone is told to smarten up a filthy vessel tied up in harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' suggests a moored boat but means cutting the end off RANK.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimaran is a sailing vessel with three parallel hulls, one kind of boat.

clue.text: There's nothing in it for cleaner

definitions.meaning: a space empty of all matter, even air
the household appliance that sucks up dust, in British usage

explanation.surface: The cleaner was cleared of blame: the accusation had nothing to it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an empty space devoid of matter and, in Britain, a household suction appliance for floors.

clue.text: Gas emitted by people in bed?

definitions.text: Gas emitted by people in bed?

parts.words: Gas emitted by people in bed?
parts.note: gas is slang for chatter, so this is the chatter of couples between the sheets, not something less polite

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means intimate conversation between lovers in bed, and gas is idle talk.

clue.text: Stated function for token

indicators.note: stated means spoken out, so the word for the function is heard rather than seen

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: Someone declares what a symbol is for in a ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: A token is an outward mark or indication of something, as in 'a token of affection'.

clue.text: Manage a day with man around home

indicators.note: around says the word for man wraps itself about the word for home

parts.note: mister is a form of address for a man
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone copes with a whole day with a husband pottering about the house.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer an organisation is to run or direct it, a straight synonym of manage.

clue.text: Developing site, friend causes possible damage

indicators.note: a site under development is being reworked, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: mate is British slang for a friend

explanation.surface: Building work on a plot, a pal worries, may cause harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damage' is slang for cost ('what's the damage?'); a builder's quote is the likely bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A builder's quotation is the probable bill, and damage is informal for the cost of something.

clue.text: Disheartened luvvy is upset with fee, strangling female in OTT manner

indicators.note: strangling means wrapping tightly round the neck, so the shuffled letters close round the abbreviation
upset tells us the letters gathered here are knocked over into a fresh order
losing its heart, the luvvy gives up one of its two central letters

explanation.surface: A theatrical darling, crushed and annoyed by the fee, overreacts by throttling a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A luvvy is British slang for a gushing, theatrical actor; losing its heart drops one of the twin Vs. 'strangling' puts the female abbreviation inside the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Effusive means gushing and unrestrained in feeling, so the adverb matches over-the-top behaviour.

clue.text: Note in former European money beside oneself

indicators.note: in says the note sits inside the money

parts.note: the franc was the currency of France and Belgium before the euro
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A banknote found in old continental currency drives someone wild with worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a banknote beside 'money', but it is the musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Being beside oneself means wild with anxiety or emotion, which is a frenzied state.

clue.text: Tool setting diamonds into stripped hazel

indicators.note: into says the abbreviation for diamonds is placed within what is left of the tree
stripped means the bark at each end of the word hazel is peeled away

parts.note: D is the card-game abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A jeweller's tool sets diamonds into a piece of bare hazel wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped' removes H and L from HAZEL, leaving AZE.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is an axe-like carpenter's implement with its blade at right angles to the handle.

clue.text: Stand that is first to sell flowers

parts.note: a dais is a raised platform or stand
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for that is

indicators.note: first to takes the opening letter of sell

explanation.surface: A market stall's priority is getting its blooms sold.
explanation.definitionFit: Daisies are small white-petalled meadow plants, examples of flowers.

clue.text: Alternative to pink fluid container

indicators.note: an alternative version of the words gives a different arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Another colour to use instead of pink paint in a jar.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small pot holding writing ink, a liquid, so it is a container for fluid.

clue.text: Asians initially in raptures, when receiving TV panel show

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letters of the next two words
receiving says the word for when takes the show's title inside it

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
QI is a long-running British TV comedy quiz panel show

explanation.surface: Fans from Asia are ecstatic when a television quiz takes them in.
explanation.walkthrough: QI (Quite Interesting) is a BBC comedy quiz hosted by Stephen Fry and later Sandi Toksvig.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq lies in western Asia, so its citizens are Asians by geography.

clue.text: View sand shifting in theatrical movement

indicators.note: shifting sand moves about, so these letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Watching the dunes move about, as if in a staged dance.
explanation.definitionFit: This dive, arms spread like wings before the plunge, is a showy, dramatic move, here called theatrical.

clue.text: Buzzer with quiet sound

parts.note: a bee is a buzzing insect
P, piano, is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: A doorbell or alarm that makes only a soft noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buzzer' wants to be the definition, a device that beeps; it is the bee.
explanation.definitionFit: A short high-pitched electronic tone is a type of sound.

clue.text: Locate part of muscle, taut: issue's back

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says only a stretch of letters inside the following words is used

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to find the bit of a tense muscle that is causing the trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Locate part' as the definition, leaving 'part of' unexplained; 'part of' is the hiding signal and 'Locate' alone defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To situate something is to place or position it, so the verb is a synonym of locate.

clue.text: Implements one used to cut fruit

indicators.note: used to cut says the numeral is put through the middle of the fruit, like a knife

parts.note: apples are fruit
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A knife is one implement used to cut fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Implements' looks like a noun for tools; it is the verb, puts into effect.
explanation.definitionFit: To implement a rule is to put it into practice, so applies is a synonym of implements.

clue.text: They're tight mass, fish in confines of cans

indicators.note: in says the mass and the fish go inside the edges of the word
the confines of the word cans are its outer letters

parts.note: a heap is a mass or pile
a skate is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Fish packed tightly in tins, like sardines.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is slang for stingy, and misers are stingy people.
